\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{جميل} (jamīl)}{جميل (jamīl)}]{\ar{جميل} (jamīl) — beautiful}

\label{lesson:AR-C86-jamil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a mistake; wrong, then the Arabic for important.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{جميل}}
\textbf{\ar{جميل}} — \emph{jamīl} — \textquotedblleft{}beautiful\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{جميل}} (\emph{jamīl}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{j-m-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to be beautiful\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Jamīl} is the \emph{faʿīl} adjective, \textquotedblleft{}beautiful\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jamīl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jamīl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{jamīl}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a mistake; wrong, then the Arabic for important, then say \emph{jamīl} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{بني} (bunnī)}{بني (bunnī)}]{\ar{بني} (bunnī) — brown}

\label{lesson:AR-C86-bunni}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for important, then the Arabic for beautiful.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{بني}}
\textbf{\ar{بني}} — \emph{bunnī} — \textquotedblleft{}brown\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{بني}} (\emph{bunnī}) is the colour of \emph{bunn}, coffee beans, with the adjective ending \emph{-ī}. Lane records \emph{bunn} as coffee berries. It is linked to Ethiopian words for coffee, such as Amharic \emph{bunna}; which way the word travelled is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for important, then the Arabic for beautiful, then say \emph{bunnī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{شهر} (shahr)}{شهر (shahr)}]{\ar{شهر} (shahr) — a month}

\label{lesson:AR-C86-shahr}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for brown, then the Arabic for a week.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{شهر}}
\textbf{\ar{شهر}} — \emph{shahr} — \textquotedblleft{}a month\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{شهر}} (\emph{shahr}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{sh-h-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to make known; the new moon\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane gives \emph{shahr} first as the new moon, named for being conspicuous, then the month; the same root gives \emph{mashhūr}, \textquotedblleft{}famous\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}
